# Studio AI Toolkit — Roster

Everything below lives at the **workspace root** (`./.claude/`) and is therefore available
from every project, every repo, and every worktree. Run Claude from the workspace root.

Agents, commands, and skills here are **project-agnostic**: they resolve what to act on
through `.claude/scripts/_project.py` and each project's `projects/<name>/project.json`.
Project-specific conventions live in `projects/<name>/AGENTS.md` and that project's own skills, never here.

## Slash commands (35)

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/add-bloc` | Add a single BLoC triplet (bloc + event + state) to an existing feature in a project's Flutter app. Use when a new operation is needed without scaffolding the full feature stack. |
| `/add-endpoint` | Add a new HTTP endpoint to a project's Go backend — handler method, route registration, service method, data access and DTOs if needed. For operations that don't fit the project's generic resource pattern. |
| `/add-usecase` | Add a single use case to an existing feature in a project's Flutter app — creates the use case class, param class, and shows where to register it in DI. |
| `/api-review` | Audit a project's Go backend code for layer violations, error handling gaps, missing validations, and convention breaches. Runs the backend-reviewer agent on changed or specified files. |
| `/arch-review` | Independent code review for a project's Flutter code — layer violations, SOLID principles, testability, and naming. Runs mobile-reviewer on staged/changed files or a specified path. |
| `/audit-performance` | Flutter performance audit for a project's app — widget rebuild waste, list rendering, main-thread heavy work, local-DB query patterns, and memory leaks. Pass a feature or path to scope, or leave empty to audit the whole presentation layer. |
| `/checkpoint` | Write the current session's progress, decisions, and verification status to durable run state so any future session can resume exactly here |
| `/codex` | Hand a task to Codex end to end — Claude writes the brief, Codex makes it (2D image or sprite, 3D model through Blender, or code), Claude reviews, sends fixes back, and delivers |
| `/copy-review` | Review and fix a project's user-facing copy across any repo (Flutter app, Next.js web, Go backend) — voice, terminology, casing, punctuation — and apply the right localization rule for that surface. Pass a path, feature name, or leave empty to check the git diff. |
| `/disk-prune` | Reclaim regenerable build artifacts across every project's repos — dry run by default, requires explicit confirmation to delete |
| `/disk-report` | Report disk usage across the whole studio workspace — reclaimable artifacts, shared cache, worktree slots, and a free-space verdict |
| `/doctor` | Health check for the whole studio AI toolkit and the docs agents depend on — roster freshness, dangling references, dead paths in AGENTS.md, hardcoded credentials, worktree/disk state, and stale runs |
| `/env-check` | Check that this machine (macOS, Linux, or Windows via WSL2 or Git Bash) has what the workspace needs — bash, git, python3, working symlinks, and each project's toolchain — and print the fix for anything missing. |
| `/hunt-bugs` | Proactive bug sweep across a project's Flutter app — static analysis, crash risks, data integrity, sync bugs, and resource leaks. Pass a feature name or path to scope the hunt, or leave empty for a full sweep. |
| `/new-feature` | Scaffold a complete Clean Architecture feature in a project's Flutter app — entity, models, mapper, datasource, repository, use cases, BLoCs, and screen. Runs senior-mobile-engineer with the project's own conventions. |
| `/new-project` | Register a new project in this workspace — scaffolds the manifest, AGENTS.md, planning/ and docs/ from templates, then wires its repos in. Pass a project name, or leave empty to be asked. |
| `/new-resource` | Scaffold a complete new resource for a project's Go backend — migration, entity, DTOs, data access, service, handler, and all registration wiring — following that project's resource pattern. |
| `/orchestrate` | Single entry point for any non-trivial task in any project — triages, routes to the right specialist agents, runs them in parallel where safe, verifies, and synthesizes one answer |
| `/plan-feature` | Generate a complete engineering implementation plan for a feature with an approved PRD in any project. Produces a layered, ordered implementation plan with every file to create or change. Use before starting implementation to align on approach. |
| `/projects` | List the projects this workspace hosts, show one project's repos and branches, or switch the active project that bare repo names resolve against. |
| `/release` | Cut a release for one repo — promote the integration branch into production (the user's call), review commits since the last tag, generate the changelog section, bump the version, tag, and hand off to the deploy pipeline |
| `/resume` | Resume an in-flight run in any project — reads durable state, reconciles it against live git, and continues from the exact point the last session stopped |
| `/review-prd` | Run a multi-role review of an existing PRD in any project. Checks product completeness (PM agent), UX quality (UX agent), and acceptance criteria testability (QA agent). Produces a single consolidated review report with prioritized gaps. |
| `/score-plan` | Score a product PRD or engineering improvement with its project's own scoring rubric (named in the <project>-planning overlay). Produces the rubric's scores with full justification, then updates the project's score index if it keeps one. |
| `/sync-feature` | Add remote sync capability (upsert + delete BLoCs) to an existing local-only feature in a project's offline-first Flutter app, following that app's existing remote BLoC pattern. |
| `/update-deps` | Safe dependency update session for any project — Flutter SDK, Dart packages, Android/iOS platform layers, Go modules, npm/Next.js packages. Reads current versions first, upgrades one layer at a time, runs analysis and codegen between each layer, and fixes all breakage before continuing. |
| `/update-tech-docs` | Update a project's technical reference documentation for a specific feature after code changes. Reads the current implementation and rewrites projects/<project>/docs/<feature>/technical-reference.md. |
| `/verify` | Run real toolchain verification (format, analyze/vet/typecheck, lint, tests) across any project's repos and report the actual exit codes — the mandatory gate before any work is called done |
| `/write-docs` | Write or update any documentation page in a project's docs (projects/<project>/docs/) — feature guides, architecture overviews, flows, setup guides, backend or web sections. Pass a topic, feature name, or doc path to scope the work. |
| `/write-prd` | Write a complete product PRD for a new feature in any project. Delegates to the product-manager agent for structure, QA agent for acceptance criteria quality, and UX agent for screen and flow requirements. Saves the result to projects/<project>/planning/features/. |
| `/wt-drop` | Remove a finished worktree after its work has landed on the repo's integration branch — verifies it is clean and merged first, then deletes the short-lived branch |
| `/wt-finish` | Finish work in a worktree — verify, generate the changelog entry, rebase onto the repo's integration branch, fast-forward it in, push, and delete the branch. No PR: feature work lands directly on the integration branch. |
| `/wt-list` | Show all active worktrees across every project — branch, size, dirty state, commits ahead of the integration branch — plus slot usage and disk verdict |
| `/wt-start` | Start new work in an isolated git worktree on a short-lived branch off the repo's integration branch (from project.json) — leaves the user's checkouts untouched and costs its source size, not GBs of build output |
| `/wt-sweep` | Retire every worktree whose work is already on its integration branch — clean, fully landed, idle — archiving its local-only files first, so disk and slots come back |

Use for security questions, focused reviews, vulnerability research, security audits, or pen tests. Run the complete workflow only for explicit codebase audit or pen-test requests, full/comprehensive/end-to-end reviews, or requested report artifacts. |
| `seo-geo` | Search (SEO) and AI-answer (GEO) visibility for every Next.js App Router web repo — metadata and metadataBase, canonical and hreflang, sitemap and robots, noindex for private and preview routes, URLs and internal links, server-rendered content and Core Web Vitals, structured data (JSON-LD), answer-first content AI engines can cite, the AI-crawler policy, programmatic pages, privacy limits, and review severities. Project domain, locales, crawler policy and page types live in the <project>-seo overlay. Load when adding or changing a public route, page metadata, sitemap/robots, structured data, or marketing content. |
| `session-continuity` | Durable run-state protocol for work in every project — how to create, update, and resume a run so any session can pick up an in-flight task after /clear, a crash, or days away. Load this at the start of any multi-step task and whenever the user says "resume", "continue", or "where were we". |
| `skill-security-auditor` | "Use before installing any skill or plugin from an untrusted source, or when asked if a skill is safe. Scans scripts, SKILL.md and dependencies for exfiltration, dangerous calls and prompt injection with skill_security_auditor.py." |
| `solid-principles` | SOLID principles applied to studio Flutter/Dart apps (Clean Architecture + BLoC) — a violation and fix for each principle, common anti-patterns, and a review quick-check. |
| `state-machine` | Renders every state of a component you choose on a throwaway page, with mock data and a switcher, so you can work on each state. |
| `ste-writing` | Write briefs, agent instructions, technical documents and every report in a controlled style based on ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English — one instruction or fact per sentence, short active sentences, one word for one meaning, conditions before actions, exact values verbatim. Covers agent dispatch briefs, AGENTS.md and skill text, runbooks, task docs, review findings, agent reports and HANDOFFs, status reports to the owner (English and Indonesian), commit messages and PR descriptions. Load before you write or review any of those. Not for user-facing UI copy (use copywriting) and not a licensed copy of the ASD-STE100 specification. |
| `storage-management` | Disk-budget rules for the studio workspace — shared build caches, worktree storage cap, safe prune targets, and the pre-flight check required before creating a worktree or running a build. Load this before creating/removing worktrees, before any full build, or whenever disk pressure is suspected. |
| `tdd` | Test-Driven Development for Flutter/BLoC Clean Architecture apps — the TDD cycle, bloc_test patterns, mocking, what to test and why, test layout, and coverage targets per layer. Project facts (mock library, test paths, fixtures, run command) live in the project's app overlay. |
| `test-case-design` | How to derive test cases for Flutter/BLoC Clean Architecture code — equivalence partitioning, boundary analysis, decision tables, state transition testing, and edge case identification per layer. Use before writing test code to ensure nothing important is missed. |
| `threejs-web` | When and how to put a three.js (WebGL) scene in a web app, including three.js as an alternative to pre-rendered motion assets (frame sequences, video, GIF, Lottie, Rive) — live glTF animation in the browser or offline rendering to video/frames — plus the decision gate before 3D, vanilla three vs React Three Fiber, client-only loading in Next.js App Router, asset formats and size budgets (glTF/GLB, Draco/Meshopt, KTX2), frame-loop and GPU performance, disposal, reduced motion and accessibility, WebGL fallback and context loss, Core Web Vitals, CSP for decoders, offline tests, and a review checklist. Load before you add, change or review any three.js, R3F or WebGL code in a web repo. For UI motion use animate; for video reels use reel-production or motion-reel. |
| `unslop` | Turns vibecoded, AI-looking UI into a designed interface with its own character. Finds a direction from the product itself, then fixes spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion in that order, and can generate a real hero visual with an image tool when one is available. Use when the user asks to unslop, polish, clean up or redesign a screen so it stops looking AI-generated, or when a UI shows the usual tells like purple gradients, glows, gradient text, emoji labels, "New ✨" badges, glossy blobs, uppercase tracked labels, pulsing elements or uneven spacing. Works on React, Tailwind, HTML and CSS, for dashboards, apps and landing pages. |
| `variant` | Builds multiple variants of a component you're working on and helps you iterate and pick one. |
| `verification` | Anti-hallucination protocol for all work in every project — evidence grades, the mandatory verification gate before claiming anything is done, and the exact vocabulary for stating uncertainty. Load this before reporting completion, before making any factual claim about the codebase, and before any agent hands off to another. |
| `wizard` | Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself. |
| `workspace-maintenance` | How this workspace's toolkit is organised — where shared, project and repo skills live, how Codex reaches them, where agents, commands and scripts go, and how to register a project. Load before adding, moving or renaming a skill, agent, command or project. |
| `workspace-orchestration` | Routing brain for work in every project — decides whether to decompose a task, which specialist agent to dispatch, what runs in parallel vs. sequence, which model tier and effort each gets, and the handoff contract between them. Load this at the start of any non-trivial task and whenever more than one repo or discipline is involved. For the specialist agents in this workspace's .claude/agents only — not Orca workers or savvy-flow. |
| `worktree-workflow` | How all new work is done in every project — in an isolated git worktree on a short-lived branch, never in the main checkouts, so the user can keep working undisturbed. Covers worktree lifecycle, the storage-safe creation path, merging into the repo's integration branch without a PR, changelog hand-off, and cleanup. Load this before starting any code change, and before creating or merging a branch. |
| `writing-for-agents` | Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. |
